transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I’m just… really drained. Like, my body feels completely worn out. Even walking in from the car, or opening the EHR at work, feels like it takes everything I’ve got.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah… I guess so. After all that energy kind of dropped off, I just started feeling really empty. Most days it feels hopeless, like I already messed up my future in healthcare before it even really started.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t really know. I haven’t been paying much attention to that, I guess. Nothing really sounds great, but… I’m not sure.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I… I don’t really know. I’ve felt pretty hopeless, but I don’t really want to get into that.
Are you having thoughts of killing yourself?
I… I’m not sure. I don’t really want to talk about that right now.
Are you thinking about killing yourself right now?
I… I don’t know. Not… not right this second, I guess. I just don’t really want to talk about it.
Have you made a plan to kill yourself?
I… I don’t know. I don’t really want to say.
Do you have access right now to something you could use to kill yourself?
I… I don’t really know. I’d rather not get into that.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or empty like this for days at a time?
I’m not really sure. I mean… maybe I’ve had bad stretches before, but I don’t know if it was like this or for days.
Before this crash in energy, was there a time when you had much more energy than usual?

Yeah… before this, I guess I did. I had a lot of energy. Like, I couldn’t really sit still at work, so I’d keep walking the halls, fixing supplies, checking rooms… just looking for stuff to do, even when I should’ve been done.
During that time, did you need less sleep than usual?
Yeah. I mean… I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours and still felt kind of wired. Lately it’s different… I’m either up before dawn worrying, or I sleep way too long and still feel wiped out.
During that high-energy time, did you feel unusually confident or powerful?
Yeah… I guess so. I kind of felt like I understood patient care better than the nurses and managers. Like if they’d just listen to me, I could fix how everything was run.
During that high-energy time, were you talking more than usual or felt like you couldn’t stop talking?
Yeah… probably. When I got going about my ideas for the clinic, I’d talk really fast, and… for a long time. People would try to cut in, but I couldn’t really stop myself.
During that high-energy time, did it cause serious problems at work or in your life?

Yeah… it got bad. I wasn’t really able to keep up at work — like, I couldn’t finish documentation safely or stay focused on the patient support stuff. Employee health ended up pulling me off and sending me for an emergency evaluation.

And I had to stop really preparing for my CNA certification too. I just… couldn’t keep up.
During that high-energy time, did you have experiences like hearing or seeing things other people didn’t, or believing things that others said weren’t true?

Yeah… a little. At work I’d hear my name over the clinic speaker, or like a monitor beeping for me, and then nobody else heard it. I’d end up going to check for a patient who… wasn’t actually calling.
About how many days did that high-energy period last?
It wasn’t just a few days… it kind of built up over maybe two months, after they changed what I was doing at the clinic.
